pattern.description: Selecting Impact as the column field instantly regroups the board: lane headers turn into green Impact-dot columns, cards re-sort into them, the toolbar button reads Impact and the picker closes, while the edit zooms back out from the dropdown close-up to the full UI.
pattern.why_premium: The zoom-out lands exactly as the board regroups, so the viewer first reads the choice up close and then sees its whole-board consequence in one continuous move, with no cut.

build_hint.gsap: Timeline: tl.fromTo('.app', {scale: 1.2, transformOrigin: '85% 15%'}, {scale: 1, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power2.inOut'}); at the same label swap board state with tl.set('.board', {className: 'board grouped-impact'}) and tl.fromTo('.card', {opacity: 0}, {opacity: 1, duration: 0.12, ease: 'none'}); tl.set('.columns-btn .value', {textContent: 'Impact'}) and tl.set('.field-dropdown', {autoAlpha: 0}).
build_hint.remotion: scale = interpolate(frame, [0, 10], [1.2, 1], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.cubic), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}) on the app wrapper with transformOrigin near the panel; render the regrouped board from the switch frame onward (hard state swap), card opacity interpolate over 3-4 frames.

notes: facts.json reports camera.move none, yet the filmstrip shows a post-production zoom-out (crop of the dropdown back to full frame, raw scale 0.842). Logged as a scale_down on the whole-UI box b01 rather than as a camera move; a human should decide whether this is really a pull_out. Board regroup is a hard state swap within one or two frames.
